figures.label: S21
figures.caption: Figure S21. (left) Ionic conductivity vs. inverse temperature plot for Sample 2 as measured by Group F. At temperatures below -75 C it is possible to de-convolute the bulk and grain boundary contributions in the impedance spectra. (right) Exemplary impedance spectrum measured at -100 C, where the grain impedance features are evident. Direct extrapolation of the grain conductivity vs. inverse temperature data estimates the upper-bound values of reported total ionic conductivities by other groups (see diamond-shaped data points at room temperature). As such, these results suggest that applied pressure during measurement is one of the main contributors for the reported spreads in ionic conductivities in this study.
